journal.en: A living geode that drinks the heat and wears the storm as armor.

chains.trait: Slow pulse of molten S₈–SO₂ internal fluid
links: Transport of metabolites in high-viscosity non-aqueous solvent

Root: Molten sulfur eutectic solvent, high viscosity, slow chemosynthesis, 3.2 bar pressure

journal.en: Its blood is liquid fire, moving with the patience of magma.

plausibility.summary: Internal circulation of a non-aqueous, vent-stable fluid matches F8 (regional S₈–SO₂ eutectic 150–250 °C) and F13 (slow H₂S/FeS₂ oxidation via SO₂ gradients). High viscosity and slow reaction rates favor visible, low-frequency pulsing rather than fast vasculature; pressure equilibration at 3.2 bar (F5) reduces implosive collapse of a tall, thin-walled tower. Closed, anoxic loop is consistent with F11. No Earth organism uses molten sulfur as blood; energy budget is necessarily low (F19). Amber IR glow from exothermic redox in the conduit is physically fine.

temperament: Stoic, vibration-sensitive, reactive to thermal spikes
secrets: Resonance Kill: High-frequency sound (whistles) matches the natural vibration mode of the siloxane lattice; sustained pitch shatters the carapace instantly.
Lattice Merging: Two Vidrio-Pulso touching for extended periods can exchange defect patterns via physical fusion, enabling horizontal gene transfer of adaptive traits.
moments: A thermal inversion drops the temperature toward 130°C. The Vidrio-Pulso's pulse slows to a crawl, its amber glow dimming. The creature folds its joints, becoming a silent, frosted statue. A Cuarzo-Sangre drifts up, sensing the residual heat signature, and rests its hollow hull against the Vidrio-Pulso's flanks. The crystal creature's dormant lattice hums faintly, sharing waste heat. The pulse returns only when a vent flares nearby, reigniting the amber heart.

journal.en: It stands as a monument to the slow chemistry of heat.
To break its crystal is to silence a million years of growth.
